subject: Post-call: gateway auth, SDK routing & structured-output retry playbook
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@novagrowth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-21T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: gateway auth, SDK routing & structured-output retry playbook

Hi Samantha — thanks again for the time today. Quick written recap to lock in next steps and the technical areas we discussed so the engineering teams can align.

Key takeaways from today's discovery:
- Nova Growth will run a small PoC (10k tokens/day) across a mix of interactive chat and batch embedding/reranker jobs.
- Primary concerns: structured-output reliability (JSON schema enforcement), auth boundary for service-to-service calls, and determinism of reranker/embeddings for repeatability.
- Target SLOs you called out: median token latency < 120ms for chat under Dedicated pool; embedding throughput ~50 reqs/sec; JSON validation failure rate < 0.1%.

Proposed technical approach (high level):
1) SDK & auth: use our SDK with API key scoped to the PoC project and mTLS optional for your VPC. We'll provide a sample service account flow and short snippet for token rotation.
2) Routing/fallback: route interactive calls to a low-latency Dedicated pool (redwood-dedicated-us1) with automatic fallback to a quantized variant if capacity constrained. Batch embedding jobs go to an embedding-optimized pool with async callbacks.
3) Structured output reliability: enforce a JSON schema at the SDK level plus a constrained-decoding policy on the model (constrained tokens + deterministic sampling). Add a validation layer that can trigger 2 retry strategies before surfacing failure: a) constrained-decoding retry with tightened beam/constraints, b) post-process sanitizer with deterministic repair.
4) Embeddings/rerankers: pin embedding model version for repeatability; store vector seeds and re-run reranker with cached candidates on schema failure.

Attachments: sample_schema_v1.json (attached) and a short routing proposal PDF.

Next steps / owners:
- Redwood: schedule a 90-minute architecture workshop (SDK + auth deep-dive) — owner: Marissa (cc'd).
- Nova Growth: confirm compliance/infosec contact and whether mTLS is required.
- Both: agree on PoC success criteria and a runbook for JSON validation failures.

Can you confirm availability for a workshop next week (Thu/Fri windows are best on our side)? If good, Marissa will drop a calendar invite and the pre-read.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call: gateway auth, SDK routing & structured-output retry playbook

Thanks Aditya — very helpful summary. A few clarifying questions from our engineering lead: 

1) For the SDK-level schema enforcement, do you run validation client-side or server-side? We prefer server-side enforcement so teams can't bypass checks.
2) If a constrained-decoding retry still violates schema, what's the behavior? Do you return the failing raw output, or do you surface a standardized error code so our service can trigger the reranker fallback?
3) For embeddings: how do you guarantee determinism across model upgrades? We want to pin a model but also understand the upgrade path.

mTLS: Procurement expects mTLS for production, but for the PoC token-based auth is acceptable. We'll confirm by EOD.

We can do the workshop on Friday 2026-08-27, 09:00-10:30 PT if that works.

— Samantha
Samantha Lee
Head of AI Platforms | Nova Growth

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@novagrowth.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-21T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: gateway auth, SDK routing & structured-output retry playbook

Great questions — quick answers + concrete behavior and a short example.

1) SDK vs server validation: We recommend a defense-in-depth approach: SDK provides a local pre-flight validator to catch obvious issues early (fast fail for developer feedback), but enforcement gate is server-side inside the Redwood control plane for the PoC. That means invalid payloads fail with a deterministic error and we only count accepted responses toward rate/usage.

2) Constrained-decoding retry behavior: our default flow is:
   a) Primary generation attempt with constrained decoding (token-blacklist + structural constraints). If the result matches schema -> return 200 with payload.
   b) If validation fails, automatically run up to 2 retry attempts with tightened constraints (lower temperature, deterministic sampling, increased beam width). Each retry is logged with attempt metadata.
   c) If retries fail, we return a standardized error: HTTP 424 with body { code: "STRUCTURE_VALIDATION_FAILED", attempts: 3, diagnostics: [short summary] } — i.e., we never silently return malformed JSON.
   d) Optional: a server-side sanitizer can attempt deterministic repairs (field coercion, missing-key insertion from defaults). That can be toggled per-route if you want graceful degradation instead of hard failure.

3) Embedding determinism & upgrades: we provide version pinning at the model and quantization profile level and a pre-upgrade snapshot tool: before changing model variants, you can run a sample set of canonical queries and compare cosine deltas. We also store embedding-seed metadata so reranker results can be reproduced. For production we recommend a weekly snapshot and a canary roll that runs old/new side-by-side for a subset of traffic.

Example SDK snippet (pseudo):
   client = RedwoodClient(api_key=env.REDWOOD_KEY, enforce_schema="server")
   resp = client.chat.create(route="redwood-dedicated-us1", schema="gs://redwood/poc/sample_schema_v1.json")

Routing/fallback note: set route policy to [preferred:dedicated-us1, fallback:quantized-lowmem-v2] with a low-latency cooldown window to prioritize consistency for interactive flows.

Workshop: Friday 2026-08-27 09:00-10:30 PT works for us. I'll send the invite with a short pre-read and an agenda covering: SDK auth flow, schema validation lifecycle, retry heuristics, and embedding determinism tests.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
